Title: Student License Policy Updates
Content: Expansion in student eligibility criteria, more students to enjoy the opportunity! We are pleased to inform you of the recent expansion in student eligibility criteria under our updated student license policy. This revision was made to enhance accessibility to the benefits of learning Marvelous Designer, thereby allowing more students to enjoy the opportunity to learn and master this valuable software at their own pace. The revised policy provides students with an affordable pricing option and an extended duration of access, allowing ample time to explore and gain in-depth knowledge of the software. Our aim is to make it easier for students to access the benefits of Marvelous Designer, encouraging them to develop and master this valuable skill set. New Policy License Option Student Yearly License: USD 99/Year (Not auto-renewal), up to 2 times within 4 years (since the first purchase) Qualification University or college A college or university that grants degrees after completing a regular course of study of at least two years (including 2-year public or private colleges and vocational schools) Primary or secondary school A licensed public or private primary, middle, or high school that provides regular education Homeschool Attendees of private CG-related courses Certification of courses more than 3 months or curriculum schedule and tuition receipt is required * Students will be asked to verify the student status through either school-issued email address or relevant documents on the purchase process. * If you have previously received a student discount, you can still benefit from the new student discount, which offers a 1-year license discount for two times. The eligibility criteria for the discount will remain the same during the checkout process. Methods of proving student qualifications Option 1. Use the email address issued by the school If you enter your school email address, a verification email will be sent to that email address. Please verify your account through the verification email. Option 2. Submit student verification documents Institution of a student If you cannot verify through your school email address, you can receive a discount by submitting one of the following documents. The submitted document must indicate your name, the name of the educational institution, and the issued date. Sensitive information such as resident registration number or grades should be removed before submission. The document must have been issued within the last six months. Student ID card Enrollment certificate or academic transcript Proof of tuition payment or statement Homeschooling student If you are a homeschool student, you can receive a discount by submitting one of the following documents. The submitted document must indicate your name, the name of the educational institution, and the issued date. Sensitive information such as resident registration number or amount should be removed before submission. Copy of home school contract Current membership ID of home school association Proof of purchase of curriculum for current academy Private CG-focused academic institution If you are attending CG-related academic institutions, you can receive a discount by submitting one of the following documents. YouTube, private streaming broadcasts, and other informal online learning will not be qualified, and only official online or offline courses with existing curricula will be qualified. Certificate of completion issued by formal institution Course program schedule (at least 3 months) and tuition receipt Notes Two-time purchase license (Not auto-renewed) When you make your first purchase, your 'student status' will be activated. The 'student status' lasts for four years, and after that, you can purchase an additional license once. You will receive two benefits over a total of four years. Once you have redeemed your student discount, you have the option to purchase a personal license. You can choose between monthly or yearly options for the personal license. Refunds are not available under any circumstances. Please make your purchase carefully. FAQ Q. Where can I purchase a student license? You can purchase a student license on the pricing page by clicking on "Buy Now." Q. How do I verify my student eligibility? By clicking on the "Get Started" button for the student license, the school email verification process will begin. An authentication email will be sent through your school email, and you can proceed with authentication through the email. If you are unable to authenticate through your school email, please proceed with authentication through "Manual Input" or "Document Submission." Q. What payment methods are accepted? You can make payments using credit cards, debit cards, and PayPal. The payment method is a prepayment for a one-year license. Q. Can I cancel my student license subscription midway? You cannot cancel your subscription midway, as it is a prepayment for a one-year license. Please choose carefully when making your purchase. Q. Can I keep my existing subscription for the student license? If you are currently subscribed to the previous version of the student license, you can keep your existing subscription. You can also take advantage of the benefits of the updated student license after your current subscription has expired. Q. Can I cancel my current subscription and purchase a new student license? If you have a current subscription, you cannot purchase a new student license before the expiration date of your current subscription. You can check the expiration date on the license page. You can purchase a new student license after the expiration date, but you will need to go through the student authentication process again. Q. How long is the validity period for the second discounted offer after purchasing a student license with the first discount offer? The validity period for the second discounted offer is four years from the date of purchase of the first discounted license. Please check your student authentication validity period on the "My Account" section. Q. If I did not use the second discounted offer within the four-year validity period of the student authentication, can I receive the student discount again for a new purchase? If you did not use all the discounted offers within the validity period of the student authentication, you cannot receive additional discounts. Please check the validity period on the "My Account" section and make sure to purchase within the validity period. Q. Does student license benefit also expire when the discount benefit expires? The four-year validity period only applies at the time of purchase. If you have purchased a student license prior to the expiration date, you may still use the license even after the expiration date has passed. For instance, if you purchase a license after applying the first discount offer on November 1, 2023, you may purchase the license with a second discounted offer until October 30, 2027, which is four years from the date of purchase of the first discounted license. Moreover, the license can be used until October 30, 2028.

Title: Auto Fitting
Content: Create Fitting Suit Objective Create a Fitting Suit for a custom avatar for Auto Fitting. Create a Fitting Suit Reference Line along the avatar surface and apply Fitting Suit. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Create Fitting Suit 3D Toolbar Create Fitting Suit Operation 1. Load your custom avatar. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 3. Create Fitting Suit Reference Line following the guide of dialogue and mouse pointer. When you have finished creating the lines, the preview of the Fitting Suit appears. 4. After creating all reference lines, press Apply button. Fitting Suit is simulated on the avatar. 5. Press Save button to save the avatar. It is saved as an avatar file(.avt) including Fitting Suit data. Note If you do not want to create symmetry, turn off Symmetry settings. If you want to recreate the reference line, select the reference line in the dialogue and press the Delete button. Auto Fitting / Re-target Draping Objective Auto Fitting Automatically adjust the size of your garment to your custom avatar and simulate the garment. Re-target Draping Simulate garment on your custom avatar. (This function maintains its original size) Location Auto Fitting Main Menu 2D Pattern Fitting Auto Fitting 2D Toolbar Auto Fitting Re-target Draping Main Menu 3D Garment Re-target Draping 3D Toolbar Re-target Draping Operation 1. Load the avatar which has completed the Create Fitting Suit process. 2. Add the garment which has Fitting Suit data. - The garment simulated on the avatar provided by Marvelous Designer (Marvelous Designer 9.5 or above) - The garment simulated on the avatar having Fitting Suit data after doing Create Fitting Suit. 3. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 4. Adjust the below options as needed in the popup window, and click OK. Maintain Pattern Curvature (%) Set the extent of deformation of pattern curvature. * Higher values will deform only the size of the pattern while preserving the existing curvature, while lower values will deform both the size and curvature of the pattern. Maintain Graphic Size ON Graphics maintain their size after auto fitting OFF The graphic is automatically resized based on the size changes of the patters. Maintain Texture Size ON Textures maintain their size after auto fitting OFF The Texture is automatically resized based on the size changes of the patters. Auto Fitting The size of the garment is automatically adjusted and the garment is simulated on your custom avatar. Re-target Draping The garment maintains its size, uv, textures and is simulated on your custom avatar. Note Before you press the Menu button, increase the particle distance of the 3D garment, which will help this function run faster. Before you press Menu button, change the property of the 3D garment to its default, which will help this function run efficiently. Show Avatar Fitting Suit (Above ver. 11) Please follow the below to see the details of an avatar fitting suit View icons on the 3D window Avatar Display Show Avatar Fitting Suit Show Garment Fitting Suit (Above ver. 11) Please follow the below to see the details of a garment fitting suit View icons on the 3D window 3D Garment Display Show Garment Fitting Suit

Title: Wind Controller Setting (Above ver. 2024.0)
Content: Objective You can add a wind effect to the 3D Window to create the impression that your garment is being affected by the wind. You can change the wind settings with several options. Location Main Menu Display Environment Show Wind Controller View icon in 3D Window Environment Show Wind Controller Operation Activate Wind Effect 1. Follow this path The wind controller appears in a 3D window in the shape of a wind. 2. Click the Wind controller A gizmo appears on the Wind controller and properties for the wind appear in the Property Editor. 3. click the checkbox under Wind Activate. The Activate checkbox will be ticked to activate the wind. 4. Click the Simulation button. Wind is activated in the 3D window. Wind Direction Setting 1. Follow this path Main menu View Environment view icon Show Wind Controller The wind controller appears in a 3D window in the shape of a wind. 2. Click on the Wind Controller The gizmo is activated. 3. Use the gizmo to adjust the position and direction of the wind, the wind flows in the direction of the icon and arrow. 4. Click Simulation. In the 3D window, the wind blows at the position and direction you adjusted. Multiple Wind Setting 1. Create or duplicate a Wind Controller. Create: Scene Browser Select Wind group, Right-click Create Wind Duplicate: Scene Browser Select Wind Controller in the Wind group, Right-click Duplicate Environment icon in 3D Window window View Wind Controller Select Wind icon in 3D window Right-click Duplicate Wind Properties Setting 1. Follow the corresponding path: Main Menu View Show Wind Controller The Wind Controller appears in the 3D Window. 2. Click the wind controller. The properties for the wind appear in the Property Editor. 3. In the Property Editor, set the wind options according to your preference. Name Changes name of the wind according to the user preference. Wind Activate Sets the activation status of the wind. Unlimited Bound It is activated by default and affects the whole space depending on its position and direction. Type Type Sets the type of the wind. Spherical: The wind blows in spherical shape, in every direction starting from the Wind Controller. Planar: The wind blows only from the designated direction, regardless of the Wind Controller's location. Strength Sets the intensity of the wind. The higher the value, the stronger the wind. Decay 0~100 Sets the range of the wind. The wind draws an arc and blows weaker according to the set value of wind intensity. If the value is "0", it blows in a straight line endlessly. Frequency (sec) Sets the cycle of the wind. The wind repeatably blows weaker and stronger in interval of set value of seconds. If the value is "0", it blows regularly. Turbulence 0~100 Sets the turbulence of wind intensity. The higher the value, the more irregular the wind intensity. Rotation Key Activate Activate to allow the wind animation rotation value to be set by the animation key. Translation X Sets Key to the X position value Y Sets Key to the Y position value Z Sets Key to the Z position value

Title: Offset as Internal Line
Content: Objective Input specific measurements to offset Patterns and segments as Internal Lines. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern Operation Offset as Internal Line Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern Right click on top of a Pattern and select Offset As Internal Line from the pop-up menu. The Offset as Internal Line window appears. Configure the settings as needed. Distance Set the interval between each Internal Line. Number of Lines Set the number of Internal Lines to be generated (ver2.4.0) Reverse Direction Offset the Internal Lines in the opposite direction. Extend Automatically extend the Internal Lines to the perimeter of the Pattern. Click OK. The offset Internal Lines appear in the 2D window. Offset as Internal Line along Curve (ver3.2.0) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern Select the two Pattern outlines between where the Internal Lines are created. Right click on the selected Pattern outline and select Offset as Internal Line along Curve. The Distribute Internal Line between Segment window appears. Adjust the options below as needed, then select OK. Name Description Number of Offsets Set the number of Internal Lines to be created. Offset Set the distance between each Internal Lines. Distance to Segment Edge Set the distance from the Pattern outlines for the Internal Lines. - Reverse Direction Horizontally reverse the Internal Lines' position based on the Distance to Segment Edge. - Opposite Segment Vertically reverse the Internal Lines' position based on the Distance to Segment Edge. Straight Create Internal Lines as straight lines. Perpendicular Direction Create Internal Lines perpendicular to the selected Pattern outlines. Internal Lines are created based on the above settings. Note: Using the same function, additional Internal Lines can be created between Internal Lines. When the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines are divided in multiple segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to select them all.

Title: Simulation
Content: Objective Use this function to apply gravity and drape Garment Patterns in the 3D Garment window. Pressing the Simulate button causes all Garment Patterns to fall toward the floor and drape onto Avatars and similar objects that are in the way. When setting seamlines between Garment Patterns, the fabric drapes and decreases as one sews the set seamlines. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Simulate 3D Toolbar Simulate Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Simulate 3D Toolbar Simulate 3D Garments in the 3D window drapes on Avatars. When the Simulation is activated, the tool automatically switches to the Select/Move tool (ver5.1.0.) Note: Simulation presets are added to the 3D toolbar (ver3.2.0). Hold down the Simulate tool to access the additional options. Name Description Simulate (GPU) (ver5.1.0) Select Simulate (GPU) for faster Simulation when working on a 3D Garment. When selected, the Simulation speed improves depending on the computer's graphic card specification. Note: * As the collision is calculated with a different algorithm when using GPU for simulation, the simulation results created with CPU and GPU are different. * This feature is to be further developed and is not suitable for use in Animation Mode yet. * This feature is only available in Windows. * This feature is only usable in a computer with NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960 or higher graphic card. Simulate (Normal) Select Simulate (Complete) after finishing a 3D Garment. When the Simulation preset is set to Simulate (Complete), Garment simulation is more defined, but the simulation speed may decrease. Simulate (Complete) Select Simulate (Complete) after finishing a 3D Garment. When the Simulation preset is set to Simulate (Complete), Garment simulation is more defined, but the simulation speed may decrease. Simulate (Complete Nonlinear) Select Simulate (Complete Nonlinear) after finishing a 3D Garment. When the Simulation preset is set to Simulate (Complete Nonlinear), Garment simulation is more defined, and fabric stretch is expressed more realistically. Adjustments to 2D Patterns' points and segments are reflected in the 3D window in real-time (ver4.2.0). The real-time Simulation (Interactive Editing) is unavailable from Marvelous Designer ver4.2.0's last patch. Simulate (GPU)

Title: Avatar Skin Offset Setting
Content: Objective Avatar Skin Offset refers to the distance between the avatar's body and garments. As the avatars and garments are composed of mesh, the avatar's body may penetrate and show through garments if the avatar's Skin Offset is low (when the distance between avatar's body and garments is close) and the Particle Distance is large. To prevent this, the avatar's default Skin Offset is set to 3mm, which is suitable for garment production. Lower the Skin Offset value for precise fitting measurement or for detailed Simulations when producing form-fitting garments. Note: Lowering the Skin Offset lowers the Particle Distance to prevent penetration of garments and also lowers the Simulation speed. It is preferable to keep the default value when working on the garments and once it is done, lower the value and Particle Distance together for fit checking or to use it as an image. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select Avatar Property Editor Skin Offset Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select Avatar Property Editor Skin Offset Enter desired value between 0~100. Click Simulate to simulate according to the set value.

Title: Move/Rotate Pattern with Gizmo
Content: Objective Move or rotate Patterns, objects, Avatar Joints and etc. with the Gizmo. Location Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard Note: Preferences for the Divided Gizmo can be accessed via: Main Menu User Setting 3D Gizmo Divided Gizmo Operation Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard The Gizmo appears. Move by dragging in a desired direction. Note: Move Y Axis Click &gt Drag the green arrow (pointing up) up and down to move the Pattern vertically. Move X Axis Click &gt Drag the red arrow (pointing right) left and right to move the Pattern horizontally. Move Z Axis Click &gt Drag the blue arrow (pointing forward) forward (upwards on the screen) or backwards (downwards on the screen) to pull or push the Pattern to the front and back. Yellow Square Box Free drifting to horizontal/vertical directions. Rotate Follow the indicated guideline below: Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard The Gizmo appears. Mouse over the Gizmo's rotation axis. The mouse cursor shape is now being replaced to (Rotate). Click Drag in the desired direction to rotate the corresponding object. Note: Rotate Y Axis Click &gt Drag the green radius left and right to rotate the Pattern centered on the vertical line. Rotate X Axis Click &gt Drag the red radius up and down to rotate the Pattern centered on the horizontal line. Rotate Z Axis Click &gt Drag the blue radius the Pattern with the central point as the axis.

Title: Can I try before I buy?
Content: For personal users: Yes, we provide a 14-days free trial. Check our free trial page for more information. * The free trial is available for a one-time use. * If you choose the monthly subscription option, automatic monthly billing will commence after the expiration of the 14-day free trial. * If you choose the annual prepayment option, there will be no automatic billing after the 14-day free trial expiration. Please purchase the annual prepayment license from the pricing page. * If you choose the student option, there will be no automatic billing after the 14-day free trial expiration. To purchase a student license, student verification is required. For more details, refer to the Student License Manual. For Enterprise users: Using the End User ID created with the Company ID, you can download the free trial by clicking the Free Trial button at the top right. (End User login required) * The free trial is available for a one-time use. * To learn how to create an End User ID using the Company ID, please refer to the Team Console Manual.

Title: Bond
Content: Objective Add bonding effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). Location Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Bond Operation Select a pattern or an internal shape to express bonding with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Bond The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent orange color. By default, the same physical property as the selected Pattern/Internal Shape is now being added to the selected Pattern/Internal Shape. Activate the Simulate. The bonded area is now being displayed stiffer as if an interlining has been fused. Repeat the first step again. In the Property Editor, select a desired preset to change its physical property. For more detailed adjustments, click on Detail. The lists on the drop-down menu are the same as Fabric's.

Title: UV EDITOR MODE: Edit UV location
Content: Editing location of UV. (ver. 7.5) Arraying individual UV Objective Arraying selected individual UV. Location UV editor mode UV right-click popup menu Operation Align Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle, Bottom Selected UVs will be aligned by a selected standard. Align menu will be displayed when selecting more than two UVs. Flip Horizontally Selected UV will be flipped left and right. Flip Vertically Selected UV will be flipped up and down. Fit UV to 0-1 Selected UV will be aligned to 0-1 coordinates. (ver. 10) * Length (Absolute): the actual distance * UV Coordinate (Relative): The ratio of 0-1 length to 1. The maximum distance is 0.4. Arraying all UV Objective Arraying all UV visible in UV editor mode. Location UV editor mode Right-click on background Operation Fit All UV to unified (0-1) All UV will be aligned to 0-1 coordinates. Tile padding option Set the distance between the pattern and the outline in the dialog. * Length (Absolute): the actual distance * UV Coordinate (Relative): The ratio of 0-1 length to 1. The maximum distance is 0.4. Set UV from pattern alignment Location of all UV will be re-arranged as 2D pattern window. Zoom Extents All Set the view in the UV window to reveal all patterns. (ver. 10) Show Wire Disable texture and show mesh view. (ver. 9.5 below) UV Packing Objective The selected UV shells can be automatically packed into the targeted UV tile. Location UV Editor Toolbar UV Packing Operation Select desired UV shells to be packed. - Ctrl+A can be used to select all existing UV shells. Follow the dedicated path found in Location above to open Dialog box: Padding Set the interval between UV shells. Unit: Permille () of UV tile size. Min: 0.001 ~ Max: 0.999 Packing Ratio The percentage of area occupied by UV shells, compared to the size of the selected UV tile. Min: 80 ~ Max: 99 * 95% is the recommended input value. Higher values take more time to pack the UV shells. Rotation Allow UV shells to be rotated if needed. Fix Scale Ratio Fix the current ratio of UV shells. UV Area Set the target UV tile to pack the selected UV shells. Reset Reset all inputs in dialog box to default. Apply All inputs will be applied to the UV shells and tiles. Close Close the dialog box

Title: 3D File (COLLADA) Import
Content: Objective COLLADA is a commonly used 3D application format that can be exported from 3D tools such as 3DS Max, Maya, Poser, and DAZ Studio and used as Marvelous Designer Avatar or Scene/Prop. For 3DS Max or Maya, install the OpenCOLLADA plugin (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenCOLLADA/wiki/OpenCOLLADA-Tools) and use it to export in COLLADA format, instead of using the default COLLADA exporter. COLLADA files contain Geometry and Material, in addition to Rigging, Skinning, and Animation data. Avatar Motion Data can be imported into Marvelous Designer in COLLADA file format, then saved as a *.mtn file, which is Marvelous Designer's proprietary format. Location Main Menu File Import OpenCOLLADA Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Import OpenCOLLADA The Open File window appears. Select the desired file and click OK. The Import COLLADA window opens. Select the settings as needed and click OK. Object Type Import as Avatar Morphs the original object into the object designated as the Morph Target. Enter the Transition Frame count into the Morphing Frame Count. The higher the frame count, the slower the morphing process. Import as Prop/Scene The simulated object passes through the Garments due to a lack of collision. Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being imported when a value is entered Garment Position Move Garment to Start Position Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). Note: If the COLLADA file path includes # (symbols), the file may not load properly.

Title: Merge Points on Internal Lines
Content: Objective Join or merge two open points on Internal Lines. Note: When a point on the Internal Line is open, it is hollow, whereas when a point on the Internal Line is closed, it is filled. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Operation Join Overlapping Points Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Select overlapping points and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Join Overlapping Points. Two overlapping points are joined and closed. Merge to Point Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select two points on Internal Lines to be merged. Right click on the point which the other point should be merged to. When the pop-up menu appears, select Merge to Point. The point is merged to the right-clicked point. Merge to Average Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select two points on the Internal Lines to be merged. Then, right click on either point to access the pop-up menu and select Merge to Average. The selected points are merged to their average point. Intersect &amp Merge Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select two points to be merged. Right click on the points to access the pop-up menu and select Intersect &amp Merge. The selected points are shortened or extended maintaining their current slope and are merged where they intersect.

Title: Automatically Create Fitting Suit at Import
Content: Objective Automatically generate a Fitting Suit for a custom bipedal avatar at import. Location Main Menu File Import OBJ/FBX Auto Create Fitting Suit. Operation Select the tool/menu indicated above under "Location". Select either OBJ or FBX file format for import. Navigate to the file location for a custom bipedal avatar (two arms, two legs, no tail) in either A-Pose or T-Pose, and double-click on the file name. The Import OBJ/FBX pop-up Window appears. Make sure the Load Type is set to Open and the Object Type is set to Avatar. Check the option box next to Auto Create Fitting Suit Click on OK. The Avatar is imported into the scene and a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the process.

Title: 3D Garment View Controls
Content: Zoom in and change view in the 3D window at once. Change Camera View Right click on the 3D window to access the pop-up menu. Select the desired view among Front, 3/4 Left, Back, Left, Right, 3/4 Right, Top, Button, or use respective shortcuts (2, 3, 8, 6, 4, 1, 5, 0) to change camera view instantly. Note: Camera Direction Change Standards Using the corresponding menu while the avatar is facing a different direction on the screen changes the camera's angle according to the avatar. Zoom In/Out Shortcuts Zoom In: Hold down the + key on the keyboard to zoom in the 3D window. Zoom Out: Hold down the - key on the keyboard to zoom out the 3D window. Zoom to Selected Zoom in/out and rotate the 3D window using the selected Pattern or item as the focal point. Select the desired Pattern or item in the 3D window and locate Main Menu Display Viewpoint Zoom Extends All, Or press the shortcut key F to enlarge the selected object at a fixed scale at the middle and control the view according to it.

Title: Particle Distance Setting
Content: Objective Particle Distance refers to the average distance between the points that make up a Garment Pattern, in other words, size of the mesh. The Garment quality and Simulation speed depend on the Particle Distance. Therefore set the value at 20mm when making a Garment and dressing it on an Avatar for faster working process, and set it under 5mm to enhance the Garment quality once it is completed. Location Property Editor Simulation Properties Particle Distance Operation Select Pattern(s). Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Simulation Properties Particle Distance Input desired value for the Particle Distance. (Minimum '0.8' to maximum '700.0') Press Enter on keyboard to apply.

Title: Symmetrical 3D State (ver. 2024.0)
Content: Easily apply the simulation of pattern to its symmetric pattern. Steps 1. This feature only applies to patterns with Symmetrized set. 2. In the 3D window, right-click on a pattern that is set to symmetrically. 3. Select the Symmetric Arrangement menu from the right-click pop-up menu. End Result The selected pattern is transformed into a simulated version of the opposite Symmetric pattern and is symmetrically arranged relative to the origin of the grid.

Title: ANIMATION MODE: Play Animation
Content: Objective Play the recorded garment animation. Location Animation Mode Animation Editor Upper Toolbar Note Edit Animation Tools (Record) Records the motion of the avatar with the simulation of the garment (Start) Moves to the beginning of the play area. (One Frame Back) Steps one frame back (Start/Pause) Plays the play area / Pauses temporarily on the play area. (One Frame Forward) Steps one frame forward (End) Moves to the end of the play area. (Repeat) Repeats the play area. (1x) Changes the play speed. (1/4x, 1/2x, 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x) (Merge) Merge selected animation layers into a single layer. (Cut) Split animation layer at current timeline position. (Delete) Deletes animation layer or Keyframe depending on selection. (Create Key) Creates new keyframe at current timeline position. (Simulation Quality / Type) Animation (Stable) Normal (Default) Custom (Simulation Quality / Value) The value is set on 1 by default. More value increases the detail of the recording. (Settings) Animation settings pop-up menu Frame Rate Simulation Quality Play Type Playback Start/End Scene Timewarp Unit

Title: License Key Update With Dongle
Content: License Key Update Objective Set the dongle key when the Network License users want to update their dongle key info. (Currently only available on Windows PC) Operation A C2V file is a file sent from the users to the Marvelous Designer Support Team and a V2C file is the other way around (sent from MD back to user). This method enables the users to update their account info / product type / the number of licenses without changing the HASP dongle key. Preparations HASP dongle key Update_License.exe file C2V file V2C file 1. Creating a C2V file 1. Plug the HASP Key (dongle) into your computer. 2. Download and execute the the RUS executable file located at the bottom of this post. 3. Create C2V file by clicking on Collect Information as below. 4. Once the C2V file successfully created, a message will be printed as below. 5. Submit your C2V file through this page (Logging in with your Company ID is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com 2. Updating a License Key using V2C file 1. Download the V2C file sent from Marvelous Designer Support Team. 2. Click on the link below to access the ACC Page, then select Update/Attach in Options on the left. ACC Page Link 3. Click Choose File to find and select the downloaded V2C file. 4. Click Apply File. 5. If the update is successful, the following message will be printed. 3. Double checking on updated License Key If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1. Open a web browser and access to http://localhost:1947 2. Make sure all the information is in this part. 3. Click Features once you see the key info. 4. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed correctly.

Title: Show Line Length
Content: Objective Show or hide all or selected Pattern line length. Location Main Menu Display 2D Pattern Show Line Length Right Click Pop-Up menu (on 2D Window) Show Line Length All Pattern line length appear on the 2D window. Note: When you select on Pattern outlines or Internal Lines, the line length show automatically. Or, you can check the selected line length, by navigating to the Property Editor 2D Line Length after selecting a segment.

Title: 3-Version-Back Update/ Trade-In Policy
Content: 3-Version Back Policy If a version of your perpetual license is 3 versions behind from the latest version at the moment, you are eligible for a 'Version Update' or 'Trade-In'. Please note that the support for the version updates will be discontinued on March 6, 2024 (00:00PDT). Personal License Version Update: Version Update for existing perpetual license will be available up to Marvelous Designer 12. Trade-In: A trade-in purchase option will remain until December 31, 2024. You can trade in your Personal Perpetual License for a 1-year subscription. After that, the perpetual license will be retrieved and cannot be reused. Also within the period of subscription, users will be guaranteed to have full access to the latest version. Trade-In: A trade-in purchase option will remain until December 31, 2024. You can trade in your Enterprise Perpetual License for a 2-year subscription. Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Bending-Weft/Warp
Content: Objective Use Bending intensity which is the resistant against being bent, to adjust the stiffness of fabric. The higher the value, the stiffer it becomes such as denim and leather, and the lower the value, the more it becomes suitable for draping materials such as silk. The Bending intensity for the weft and warp directions can be set separately like the real fabrics. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Preset Bending-Weft/Warp Expressing materials with Weft (Horizontal) bending intensity Expressing materials with Warp (Vertical) bending intensity
